segments.en: Locals like to say there is a beach here for every day of the year. You will soon believe it, because around almost every bend of the coast waits another curve of white sand and turquoise water.

Antigua and Barbuda is a nation of two main islands in the eastern Caribbean, where the Atlantic meets the Caribbean Sea. Antigua is the bigger and busier one; Barbuda, to the north, is flat, quiet and wonderfully wild.
Many Antiguans call their island Wadadli, an old name that you will see on boats, shop signs and even the local beer. It is a word said with real affection.

The capital, Saint John's, is a harbour town of painted wooden buildings, busy markets and a white cathedral with twin towers. On market mornings, stalls are piled high with mangoes, breadfruit and sweet potatoes.
Look for the Antigua black pineapple. It stays green outside even when it is ripe, and people here will tell you it is the sweetest pineapple in the world.
The national dish is fungee and pepperpot. Fungee is smooth cornmeal, a little like polenta, and pepperpot is a thick stew of greens, vegetables and meat.

On the south coast lies English Harbour, a sheltered bay where sailing ships once hid from hurricanes. Its restored Georgian dockyard, named after Horatio Nelson, is still a working marina full of yachts.
Above the harbour, at Shirley Heights, people gather on Sunday evenings to watch the sunset while a steel band plays, and the party often carries on into the night with reggae and soca.
Cricket is close to a religion here. Antigua has given the world some legendary players, including Sir Viv Richards, and a game at the ground named in his honour is loud, joyful and full of music.
Every summer, Carnival fills the streets with costumes, calypso and steel pan, celebrating freedom from slavery. The wildest moment is J'ouvert, when bands dance through Saint John's at dawn.
On Barbuda, parts of the shore glow a soft pink, and in Codrington Lagoon thousands of frigatebirds nest. The males puff out bright red throat pouches like balloons to impress a mate.
So pack your sunhat and say a friendly good morning to everyone you pass, because that is the custom here. Then sail west across the channel, where Saint Kitts and Nevis is waiting on the horizon.
